title: Copying joined fields
statement: For every type $\Gamma$ and natural number $m$, there is a natural-number constant $C$ such that the following holds for every input word $x$, list of words $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ over $\Gamma$, and starting configuration $d$ of the specified two-tape machine. If tape 0 stores the joined fields throughout offsets $-1$ through the joined-fields length, tape 1 is blank throughout that interval, and the machine starts in its designated entry state, then it reaches its exit state at some time $t\le C(L+1)$, where $L$ is the joined-fields length. The exit state is avoided at every earlier time, both work-tape heads remain within distance $C(L+1)$ of their initial positions throughout the run, and at the final time tape 1 stores the joined fields in the interval of length $L$ beginning at its initial head position while all other tape contents and configuration data are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Initial state is the designated copy entry state
Tape 0 satisfies the joined-fields record condition on offsets $-1$ through $L$
Tape 1 is blank on offsets $-1$ through $L$
